ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1993 (including the ultimate beneficial ownership and control reporting regime and associated regulations), Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, Privacy Act 2020, and the AML/CFT Regulations 2011

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille Convention states: have the certificate certified by a New Zealand Notary Public if a certified copy is required, then apply to the New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) Authentication Unit for a Hague Apostille. For non-Apostille states: notarize, then obtain DIA authentication, then submit to the destination-state embassy or consulate for Consular Legalization. The Hague Apostille and Consular Legalization paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague path: DIA Apostille after notarization of any certified copy. Non-Hague path: DIA authentication followed by Consular Legalization at the relevant New Zealand diplomatic mission or the destination-state consulate in Wellington. Apostille and Consular Legalization are alternative and mutually exclusive authentication methods.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised Board Resolution and Power of Attorney executed by all directors and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Duly appointed board of directors of the New Zealand company; signatures to be notarised by a New Zealand Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague member-state destination: notarise signatures, then obtain DIA Apostille. Non-member-state destination: notarise signatures, obtain DIA legalisation, then prescribed Consular Legalization at the destination mission. Never commence Consular Legalization after an Apostille has been issued for the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Company Constitution (Articles of Association) adopted under the Companies Act 1993
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and shareholders, with a certified true copy by the New Zealand company secretary or a New Zealand lawyer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague path: notarization of the certified copy, then DIA Apostille. Non-Hague path: notarization, DIA authentication, then Consular Legalization by the destination-state consulate. Apostille and Consular Legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; an Apostille cannot be upgraded to Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter / banker's know-your-customer and customer due diligence confirmation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A registered New Zealand bank authorised under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989, issued after successful account opening and enhanced due diligence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague countries: issue on bank letterhead, notarise by a New Zealand notary if required, then obtain DIA Hague Apostille. Non-Hague countries: notarise, obtain DIA legalisation, then destination-state Consular Legalization. The two authentication chains are mutually exclusive alternatives.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, UBOs, authorised signatories, counterparties, and beneficial controllers must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the New Zealand targeted financial sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, the United Kingdom HM Treasury sanctions list, and the United States OFAC SDN and Section 5612 lists, together with global PEP databases. Because the target industry is a Medium-Risk Enhanced data-pipeline API business, enhanced due diligence is mandatory for beneficial owners with political exposure, including negative news and adverse media screening, source-of-wealth verification, and transaction monitoring. Any match or ambiguous hit triggers escalation to the AML/CFT compliance officer and filing of a suspicious transaction report under Part 3 of the AML/CFT Act 2009, and no step may proceed until the risk is cleared.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register online name search and incorporation portal (https://www.companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory requirement: every token must be in Latin script; Chinese, Cyrillic, or other non-Latin characters are not permitted in the registered company name unless a phonetic Latin transliteration is supplied and passes the Register's phonemic equivalence algorithm. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) distinctive core element unique within the Companies Register; (2) descriptive industry element connected to the actual business and not misleading; (3) mandatory legal suffix 'Limited' or 'Ltd' for a limited company; and (4) a sequential numeric or alpha disambiguator only when tiers (1)-(3) are unavailable due to identical-name conflicts. Maori macrons and diacritical marks are recognised, and transliteration must use standard New Zealand English orthography.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 10 working days of a Companies Office name-rejection decision, the applicant or incorporated law firm must submit a formal reconsideration request to the Registrar of Companies under the name clearance provisions of the Companies Act 1993, explaining why the proposed name is not identical or almost identical to a name on the Companies Register, why it is not misleading, deceptive, or offensive, and why any sensitive token does not require prohibited ministerial approval under the relevant licensing statute. The request must include the Companies Office reference number, proposed name, certificate of character search, and supporting consent or exemption evidence. If the Registrar affirms the rejection, the applicant may apply for judicial review to the High Court under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016, ordinarily within 28 days; alternatively, the applicant may amend the distinctive core token and file a clean incorporation application. A name reservation may not be extended, but a fresh reservation may be filed after the prevailing reservation window expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Companies Act 1993 requires a registered office that is a physical address in New Zealand, open to the public and accessible for service of documents; a PO Box alone is not a registered office. A virtual office or commercial mailbox can be used only as a service address if a separate physical New Zealand business address exists and is disclosed to the Registrar and Inland Revenue. For an ISIC 6201 web-scraping and proxy API business, local New Zealand banks will generally reject a mailbox-only arrangement for account opening and will require director presence or a local office address. Inland Revenue will also treat an offshore-controlled virtual office as weak evidence of tax residence and may re-characterise income as managed from offshore, so a virtual office is not commercially advisable for this company if it seeks a New Zealand corporate identity and tax treaty protection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) verify that the registered office equals the street address disclosed to the Companies Office and is not a postal forwarding address; (2) maintain board minute book, share register, UBO register, and original constitutions at that address; (3) ensure a welcoming sign and administrative personnel are present during normal business hours; (4) file annual returns on time; (5) preserve accounting records and supply invoices/proxy gateway contracts. Quantified risk: low at 5-10% per year for an ordinary online-software company, but enhanced to 15-25% where the registered office is a virtual suite used by non-resident controllers, because the Companies Office and Inland Revenue periodically cross-check addresses on high-risk AML categories and may perform unannounced site visits in Auckland or Christchurch if the UBO profile is not transparent.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act No 105 of 1993), as amended; principally sections 12, 14, 16, 18, 32, 42, 87, 122, 127, 128, 151, 189, 220, 232 and 336, together with the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and the Companies (Register of Companies) Regulations 2017; the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 is not triggered for a non-offering private limited company unless a public offer is made.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company filed electronically through the New Zealand Companies Office Register a Company portal, resulting in a Certificate of Incorporation and automatic New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) allocation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Companies Act 1993 imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement for a New Zealand limited company; shares may be issued for nominal or nil consideration and there is no escrow, blocked capital account, or bank statement verification requirement for incorporation. Directors must, however, comply with solvency requirements before any distribution or share buy-back and must maintain an accurate share register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF PLACEHOLDER LIMITED; RESOLVED, by the Board of Directors of the Company, at a duly convened meeting of the Board held on PLACEHOLDER DATE, at which a quorum was present throughout, and passed by unanimous vote of all directors in attendance, that: ONE: The issue and allotment of PLACEHOLDER NUMBER ordinary shares of no par value in the capital of the Company, at an issue price of NZD 0.01 per share, to the persons set out in the register of shareholders, be and is hereby approved, ratified, and confirmed, and the directors are authorised to receive the subscription moneys and to certify that the shares are fully paid in cash or as contributions in kind as stated in the subscription statements; TWO: The registered office of the Company at PLACEHOLDER STREET, PLACEHOLDER CITY, New Zealand, and the address for service in New Zealand at PLACEHOLDER ADDRESS, be and are hereby adopted as the Company's registered office and address for service under the Companies Act 1993, and the directors be and are hereby authorised to file all necessary notices and registrations with the New Zealand Companies Office; THREE: The bank selected by the Managing Director, being any licensed bank in New Zealand, be and is hereby authorised to open and operate bank accounts in the Company's name, and the directors, officers, and other persons identified in the banking mandate be and are hereby appointed as authorised signatories, with power to sign, execute, endorse, and deliver cheques, drafts, payment orders, electronic wire transfers, stablecoin and digital asset settlement instructions, foreign exchange contracts, letters of credit, and all related financial instruments, on such terms and subject to such dual-signature and transaction limits as the Board may approve; FOUR: PLACEHOLDER NAME be and is hereby appointed Chairperson of the Board, PLACEHOLDER NAME be and is hereby appointed Managing Director, and PLACEHOLDER NAME, if required by the Company's constitution, be and is hereby appointed Secretary of the Company, each to hold office until removal or until the conclusion of the next annual shareholders' meeting in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the constitution; FIVE: The Managing Director and the officers of the Company be and are hereby authorised and empowered to file, sign, deliver, and prosecute all registration forms, tax applications, banking facilities, agreements, and ancillary documents necessary to give full effect to these resolutions, including applying for the New Zealand Business Number, Inland Revenue Department registration, goods and services tax registration, and any digital data-processing or API-related consents required under New Zealand law; SIX: All prior acts of the incorporators, shareholders, and provisional directors in relation to the incorporation and establishment of the Company be and are hereby ratified, adopted, and confirmed in all respects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation corporate structure, director consent, and document package
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: No government filing at this stage; internal corporate action by founding shareholders, provisional directors, and New Zealand legal counsel; notarization and apostille where documents will be used abroad.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect certified true copies of passports, government-issued identification, proof of residential address, and beneficial ownership documents for each shareholder and director. Decide whether the company will adopt a constitution or rely on the default rules of the Companies Act 1993. Verify that at least one director is a New Zealand resident or an Australian resident who also holds a directorship in a New Zealand company, as required for a company carrying on a substantive New Zealand operation. Confirm the proposed company name does not conflict with names on the New Zealand Companies Register. Prepare signed consents to act as director, share subscription agreements, and a shareholders' agreement if required. Determine the initial share allotment, registered office address, and address for service in New Zealand. Cause all signature pages to be witnessed and, if the beneficial owner or director executes outside New Zealand, notarized and apostilled.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of passports or government-issued identification for every director and shareholder
Proof of residential address, dated within the last three months
Proposed company constitution, if any
Signed consent to act as director for each proposed director
Share subscription agreement or shareholders' agreement
Ultimate beneficial ownership chart and declaration for any trust or corporate holding structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any identification document or director consent is queried, have the document re-notarized and apostilled within five business days and resubmit through counsel; if the proposed New Zealand resident director is unavailable, appoint an alternative resident director before filing the incorporation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name sufficiency check and incorporation filing with the Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; online submission using RealMe login through the Register a Company portal; the Registrar of Companies issues the Certificate of Incorporation and the New Zealand Business Number.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a free name search on the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm the preferred company name is available and not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. Access the Companies Office online portal, complete the electronic application for registration, enter the proposed company name, registered office address, address for service, director details, shareholder details, and the initial share allotment. Attach the constitution if the company has adopted one, together with signed director consents and any required authority forms. Pay the prescribed filing fee electronically. The Registrar will register the company under the Companies Act 1993, issue a Certificate of Incorporation, and automatically allocate a New Zealand Business Number. The company is legally extant once the certificate is issued, and the directors must then formalize the statutory registers.
required_dossiers: Completed electronic application for registration
Preferred company name and name availability search result
New Zealand registered office address and address for service details
Full names, dates of birth, nationality, and residential addresses of all directors and shareholders
IRD numbers of directors, or an accompanying application to Inland Revenue
Signed constitution, if adopted
Statement of share capital and initial share allotment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the name or requests corrections, respond through the Companies Office portal within ten working days, amend the offending field, and resubmit; if the name is refused because of similarity to an existing mark, select a distinguishable alternative name and file a new application under the same incorporation intention.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Department registration, IRD number, GST, and employer obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue); online business registration through the MyIR portal and the New Zealand Business Number registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation, then enrol the company with Inland Revenue for income tax purposes. Register for goods and services tax if the company expects annual taxable supplies to exceed NZD 60,000, or voluntarily if it wishes to claim input credits immediately; register for PAYE if any employees will be engaged. Supply the company's actual or estimated turnover, business activity description identifying ISIC 6201 computer programming and public commercial web scraping API services, proposed balance date, and director information. Inland Revenue will issue the company's IRD number and confirm filing obligations. The company must maintain a New Zealand address for service and keep all tax records in English. If the directors are non-resident, provide their overseas IRD numbers and a New Zealand contact person to support verification.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
NZBN confirmation
IRD number application including director IRD numbers or foreign tax identification numbers
Estimated annual turnover and business activity description for ISIC 6201
Registered office and address for service confirmation
GST registration election, if applicable
Director identification and residency evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue issues a discrepancy notice, provide corrected shareholder and director information through MyIR within fifteen working days and submit a statutory declaration if the original identity details were ambiguous; if the application is suspended for failure to verify a director, submit a certified copy of the director's passport and proof of residential address and request expedited clearance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate bank account opening, payment rail onboarding, and AML/CFT due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed New Zealand bank selected by the board, such as ANZ, ASB, BNZ, or Westpac, acting under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 additionally the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 if a non-bank payment provider is used.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the fully executed board resolution, certificate of incorporation, NZBN confirmation, IRD number confirmation, statutory register extracts, director and shareholder identification, beneficial ownership declarations, and source of funds documentation to the chosen financial institution. The bank will risk-rate the company as medium enhanced because the business is a public commercial web scraping and proxy API gateway handling payment rails including Stripe and USDC. Provide the bank with the expected transaction profile, counterparty categories, target markets, website or API documentation, data usage policies, and anticipated monthly volumes. Execute the corporate account mandate, specifying signatories, dual-signature thresholds, and settlement instructions for fiat and stablecoin payments. If USDC is to be accepted, the bank may require a separate digital asset payment processor relationship with full AML/CFT policies and transaction monitoring.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NZBN confirmation
Pro-forma board resolution authorizing bank accounts and signatories
AML/CFT and know-your-customer forms for all signatories
Ultimate beneficial ownership declaration and source of wealth explanation
Business plan and transaction projections for API data services
Executed corporate banking mandate
Compliance policy describing lawful scraping practices and privacy safeguards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a due diligence request, respond within five business days with a corporate group structure chart, client contracts, and evidence of lawful data sources; if the application is declined because of industry risk, apply to a second licensed New Zealand bank or engage a registered non-bank payment services provider that offers Stripe and USDC settlement rails and obtain a fresh board resolution approving the alternative provider.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation governance, statutory registers, annual return, and data-protection compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Inland Revenue, and the board of directors; Privacy Act 2020 compliance is handled by the appointed privacy officer if personal data is processed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within ten working days of incorporation, prepare and maintain the statutory registers required by the Companies Act 1993, including the register of shareholders, register of directors, share allotment records, and minute books. Issue share certificates and record all transfers or allotments. File the first annual return before the expiry of thirteen months from incorporation and thereafter annually, updating the registered office, addresses for service, and director details with the Registrar. Review financial reporting obligations under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; small companies may adopt simplified reporting, but full accounting records must be kept in English. For the digital web scraping and proxy API business, assess whether the company receives personal data; if so, appoint a privacy officer, maintain a privacy statement, and comply with the Privacy Act 2020. No industrial or environmental operating permit is triggered, but office tenancy and health and safety at work obligations under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 must be observed.
required_dossiers: Share register and register of directors
Registered office file and address for service confirmation
Minutes of board and shareholders meetings
Share certificates and allotment records
Annual return checklist and shareholder information
Financial statements and accounting records
Privacy impact assessment, privacy policy, and privacy officer appointment if personal data is processed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a late annual return notice or threatens removal, file the annual return online immediately and pay any late filing fee; if the company has already been struck off, apply for restoration under the Companies Act 1993 within twenty business days, provide a full explanation and updated director consents, and pay the reinstatement fee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the declared business is an ISIC 6201 computer programming / data-pipeline API service; there is no factory, chemical plant, assembly line, or warehouse requiring an industrial licensing board or municipal manufacturing permit in New Zealand.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no mandatory industry operating permit is required for a pure digital public commercial web scraping and proxy API gateway business.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - any physical development would otherwise fall under the regional council and the Resource Management Act 1991; no national Environmental Protection Authority involvement is triggered by a digital API service.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no physical construction, land-use change, discharge, or resource consent trigger exists; no full EIA report or environmental registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater, VOC, particulate, hazardous waste, or effluent thresholds apply; office waste must be disposed of in accordance with local council by-laws, and any electricity or generator use must comply with ordinary building and utility regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defence fire permit, structural load inspection, or workplace occupancy approval is required for a remote software/API operation; the entity must still comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, standard electrical safety standards, and any building-code requirements applicable to an administrative office lease.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Taake) - IRD - operating through the myIR Secure Online Services portal (myir.ird.govt.nz); company registration is administered by the New Zealand Companies Office with the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident limited company, the IRD number constitutes the statutory Tax Identification Number. The non-resident entity must first obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) via the Companies Office where a local registration is created, then apply to Inland Revenue through the myIR online tax registration workflow or an IRD paper application pack. The application must include the certificate of incorporation, constitution or equivalent charter documents, registered office details, director and ultimate beneficial owner identification, non-resident ownership schedule, and a declaration of the New Zealand taxable activity or offshore remote-services nexus. If the entity has no physical presence or employment connection in New Zealand, a New Zealand tax agent or legal representative is expected to be appointed to receive IRD notices and service documents. IRD will issue the IRD number and, where warranted, a GST registration number after the taxable activity nexus under the GST Act 1985 and Income Tax Act 2007 is established.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. New Zealand does not recognise a US-style check-the-box election or any general ordinary-income pass-through election; a limited liability company is mandatorily taxed as a separate entity under the Income Tax Act 2007. The base erosion and profit shifting hybrid mismatch rules in the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 apply automatically and are not election-based.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of GST taxable supplies made in New Zealand in any 12-month period; for a non-resident offshore supplier of remote services or digital products, registration is mandatory when supplies to New Zealand consumers exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period. Voluntary registration is available below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, mandatory tax-authority API filing, or anti-fraud digital stamping regime applies in New Zealand. GST tax invoices must be issued in accordance with the GST Act 1985 and retained in records; e-invoicing may be exchanged through the voluntary Peppol interoperability framework supported by Inland Revenue. GST returns are filed electronically through myIR or accredited gateway software without transaction-level pre-clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under section 11 of the GST Act 1985, goods exported from New Zealand are zero-rated where the supplier exports the goods within 28 days of supply and retains sufficient evidence of export. Services supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand are zero-rated when the services are not directly connected with New Zealand land, property, or other goods in New Zealand. Qualifying offshore digital services, including public commercial web scraping, proxy API gateways, and data pipeline services, may be zero-rated where the recipient is a non-resident business outside New Zealand and the supply is not consumed or exploited in New Zealand. The supplier must substantiate the cross-border supply with customs, logistics, contractual, and foreign-exchange settlement evidence. Digital services supplied to New Zealand consumers are taxed at 15% under the offshore supplier remote-services rules and are not export zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Entry lodged through the New Zealand Customs Service Trade Single Window for physical exported goods
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the exporting carrier
Outward cargo manifest and port or airport export report
Commercial invoice and export or API service contract identifying the non-resident buyer and the offshore destination or consumption point
Bank foreign-exchange settlement or remittance credit advice evidencing actual receipt of offshore consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may reassess the supply at 15% GST and claw back refunds if export zero-rating is not fully substantiated, goods are not exported within the statutory 28-day window, services are in fact performed in New Zealand, or the documentation evidencing export and payment is false. The Tax Administration Act 1994 imposes shortfall penalties up to 150% for evasion or fraud, with lesser penalties for failure to take reasonable care, unacceptable tax positions, and abusive tax positions; use-of-money interest also runs on unpaid GST from the original due date. Knowledge-based false refund claims or deliberate false statements in GST returns may additionally give rise to criminal prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand administers a fully open capital and current account regime. The New Zealand dollar is freely convertible and trades without exchange control restrictions. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand does not require approvals for cross-border equity injections, trade receipts, dividend repatriation, or loan repayments. The Financial Markets Authority and the Reserve Bank supervise licensed institutions but do not impose FX surrender or convertibility restrictions. Banks may apply individual transaction vetting under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, sanctions screening, and tax information exchange protocols, but these do not obstruct legitimate treasury flows. Dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are taxable via non-resident withholding tax or approved issuer levy, but funds can be remitted in the currency of choice. The absence of exchange controls and the absence of an official exchange rate band create a stable setting for multi-currency treasury operations. Companies can hold foreign currency accounts, transact in any approved currency, and hedge currency risk through dealers without requiring central bank permission. The only practical hurdles relate to bank onboarding documentation, beneficial ownership disclosure, and ordinary commercial KYC, all of which can be satisfied with proper legal entity records. Overall convertibility is best assessed as unrestricted and at a low compliance burden by global standards.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement or fixed conversion ratio exists in New Zealand. All exporters may retain one hundred percent of export proceeds in licensed foreign currency accounts or convert to New Zealand dollars at market rates. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand does not mandate any timeline for repatriation. Exporters are nonetheless required to maintain accurate invoices and tax records for Inland Revenue, and may be sampled by Statistics New Zealand for balance of payments statistical reporting; reporting, if requested, is limited to data collection and is not a control or approval mechanism. The target entity's API subscription receipts in USD or EUR can thus be collected via Stripe or direct wire and held or converted with no mandatory FX switching window.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and NZD/USD Transactional Account
Basic Operational Currency Account with Multi-Currency Sweep Capacity
Capital Escrow Account and Foreign Currency Account
Business Operating Account / Wholesale Transactional Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs are not licensed as full New Zealand banks for taking deposits; only registered banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 can offer core transactional or deposit accounts. Non-bank financial service providers may be registered on the New Zealand Financial Service Providers Register and provide niche payment services if licensed, but offshore digital EMIs without an approved local branch or FSP registration are largely barred from servicing local entities as their primary clearing bank. For the target entity, a fintech EMI is rated Low for primary treasury clearing because most offshore EMIs cannot issue ledger entries that satisfy New Zealand Companies Office capital verification and will not provide corporate credit, FX hedging, or LC issuance. Use an EMI only as a secondary collection gateway, such as Stripe or a regulated stablecoin on-ramp, while placing all capital inflows and outbound liquidity through a Tier 1 domestic commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No universal legal mandate exists for directors to physically appear in a New Zealand branch. All four Tier 1 domestic commercial banks accept digital onboarding with video identity verification for New Zealand-based directors. However, non-resident directors and shareholders may need certified passport copies, proof of address, and enhanced due diligence interviews by phone or video. Remote consular proxy opening is not a standard product; if a proxy is proposed, the proxy must be a New Zealand-licensed legal or accounting professional holding a valid power of attorney and must satisfy the bank's identity verification protocol. Some banks require a substantive New Zealand nexus, such as a registered office, a local director, a local professional firm, or a New Zealand tax position, before opening a full operational current account. The target entity should engage a New Zealand registered agent to smooth remote onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Target sector ambiguity: the description of web scraping and API gateway services may raise Privacy Act 2020 and reputational concerns regarding data provenance and personal information handling.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete commercial due diligence pack containing licensing agreements with data source providers, written confirmation that only publicly accessible or properly licensed data is processed, Privacy Act 2020 compliance policies, customer terms of service, product architecture documentation, and a clear explanation of how ISIC 6201 and NAICS 518210 map to a lawful data pipeline business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: non-resident investors using nominee shareholders, layered trusts, or discretionary structures may create uncertainty about ultimate ownership and source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full chain of ownership diagram reaching natural persons, New Zealand Companies Office register extracts, director identification numbers, certified passport copies, recent utility bills for all UBOs, tax identification numbers, trust deed and settlor/protector declarations for any trust, and a written confirmation from a New Zealand legal advisor that no bearer shares or undisclosed nominees exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency and USDC payment rails listed as target payment rails may trigger concern about unregulated inflows, cross-border chain tracing, and potential layering through stablecoin liquidity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury policy confirming that cryptocurrency is used only for customer collection conversions through a regulated New Zealand FSP or licensed exchange, blockchain analytics reports for source addresses, exchange withdrawal confirmations, bank statements showing conversion into NZD/USD, and an irrevocable undertaking that all supplier payments and shareholder distributions will be settled via traditional SWIFT rails.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction velocity mismatch: a low-capital data API company may receive high volumes of small cross-border subscription payments, which could be misread as third-party deposits, money circulation, or trade-based layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year financial projections, audited or internally reviewed revenue model, signed client subscription agreements, payment processor reconciliation statements, billing API logs, a counterparty country restrictions policy, sanctions screening procedures, and a board-approved AML/CFT risk assessment aligned with the New Zealand medium-risk enhanced rating for this business.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital should be transmitted via SWIFT MT103 from the corporate parent or investor to the company's NZD or USD account at a Tier 1 New Zealand bank. The sender's bank must include the full beneficiary company name, New Zealand bank account number, branch code, and SWIFT BIC. The purpose of payment must explicitly state Equity Contribution or Share Subscription. For this data-API service, no consent is required under the Overseas Investment Act because the business is not acquiring sensitive land or substantial New Zealand business assets. The company must allot shares and file the share allotment return with the New Zealand Companies Office within twenty working days. Capital verification is evidenced by the bank statement, the share allotment resolution, the updated shareholder register, and, if required by the bank, a director's statutory declaration confirming that the funds are genuine paid-up share capital or irrevocable shareholder loans with written facility agreements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements for server hosting, data source licenses, overseas contractors, and legal fees should be executed through corporate internet banking using SWIFT MT103 payments with full invoice references. For high-value international merchandise or infrastructure procurement, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued under UCP600 with MT700 messages is the preferred clearing rail. Documentary collections under DP or DA terms are permissible for lower-risk settlements. Since the target entity primarily sells API access and data subscriptions, outbound flows will be recurring service payments and royalties rather than physical trade; these should be batched, reconciled, and classified under appropriate IRD tax invoice rules. Stripe and regulated payment gateways may be used for client collections, but all vendor and treasury outflows should settle through the domestic banking system to maintain audit clarity and avoid sanctions complexity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards in NZD/USD and NZD/EUR with Tier 1 New Zealand banks
FX swaps combining spot and forward legs for temporary liquidity rebalancing
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS) applied to long-term shareholder loan facilities

Vanilla FX options and option collars for cash-flow hedging; non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are technically accessible through offshore counterparties but are not necessary given full NZD deliverability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the company's annual return date, defined as the anniversary of incorporation, in respect of the period ending on the day before that anniversary; the return must be filed online no later than 18 days after the annual return date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late filing penalty accrues at NZD 10.00 (approximately USD 6.10) per day while the annual return remains overdue; the Companies Office may issue a notice of removal and, after three consecutive missed annual returns, may administratively strike the company off the New Zealand register under sections 318-319 of the Companies Act 1993, thereby terminating legal existence and triggering asset vesting in the Crown subject to restoration procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and Audit Report (if the entity is non-exempt under the Financial Reporting Act 2013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office via the Companies Register, and Financial Markets Authority (FMA) if the company is an FMC reporting entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Unless exempt as a small entity, financial statements must be prepared in accordance with New Zealand GAAP, approved by the board within 5 months of balance date, fully audited by a licensed auditor before approval, and filed with the Companies Register within 20 working days after board approval; FMC reporting entities must meet the shorter FMA annual report disclosure deadlines under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or audit statutory financial statements creates director liability under the Companies Act and Financial Reporting Act, may trigger FMA enforcement action, infringement fines, adverse audit qualifications, inability to rely on the small-company defence, and may constitute grounds for a forced compulsory audit or application by a shareholder for audit review; persistent non-compliance can be cited as a factor in a removal action by the Registrar of Companies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Event-Driven Register and Company Details Updates (director changes, registered office changes, share allotments, share transfers, and beneficial ownership movements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (for external registration), and internal statutory registers maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change of directors or registered office must be notified to the Companies Office within 15 working days of the change; share allotments or changes to issued capital must be filed with the Companies Office within 15 working days; completed share transfers must be reflected in the Register of Members within 30 days of lodgement and board approval, with a parallel update of the annual return confirmation cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Where an event is not filed, the company and each responsible director commit a continuing contravention of the Companies Act 1993 and may be prosecuted by the Registrar; summary conviction may give rise to fines up to NZD 10,000 plus a further daily fine for continuing non-compliance; a defective non-updated Register of Charges may render floating charges void against subsequent creditors, and any inaccuracy in the public register can expose the company to strike-off or to restrictions on future issuances of shares.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified CPA audit is legally mandatory for every New Zealand limited company that is not a small entity under section 46 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013. An entity is a small entity if, in each of two consecutive accounting periods, it satisfies at least two of the following criteria: (a) total assets, including subsidiaries, are not more than NZD 3 million at balance date; (b) total revenue, including subsidiaries, is not more than NZD 5 million for the accounting period; and (c) the entity employs no more than 50 full-time equivalent employees. A company that exceeds at least two of these thresholds in two consecutive years ceases to be small and must appoint a qualified auditor and file audited financial statements. An audit is also compulsory for FMC reporting entities under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, including issuers of listed equity or debt, managed investment schemes, and life insurers, regardless of size. Registered banks and licensed insurers also attract mandatory audit. In addition, even a small entity cannot avoid an audit where shareholders with at least 5% voting rights requisition an audit under the Companies Act 1993 or a statutory audit is imposed as a regulatory condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The governing framework is New Zealand generally accepted accounting practice (NZ GAAP). For-profit entities that are not small may be required to use New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS). Tier 2 for-profit entities without public accountability may apply NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR), while Tier 1 entities with public accountability or larger economic significance must apply full NZ IFRS. A small entity that prepares general purpose financial statements may apply the XRB A1 accounting framework and simplified disclosure standards issued by the External Reporting Board, and all financial statements must comply with the definitive hierarchy comprising the Companies Act 1993, the Financial Reporting Act 2013, and the applicable accounting standards approved by the External Reporting Board.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not operate a public annual UBO declaration form. The annual return filed with the Companies Office serves as the annual confirmation of company information, including the registered office, director details, shareholding structure, ultimate holding company, and statutory solvency details. Any share transfer is required to be recorded in the internal Register of Members and notified to the Companies Office within 15 working days where it results in a change of shareholding particulars; the full and definitive recording in the statutory Register of Members must be completed within 30 days of the transfer lodgement. For companies covered by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, the company must identify and verify each beneficial owner at the start of the business relationship and must maintain and refresh that beneficial ownership information on an ongoing risk-based basis; no separate annual UBO fee or filing is payable to the Companies Office for an ordinary non-listed limited company.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 to USD 650 per annum for a standard New Zealand registered office and compliance agent service; a full corporate secretarial retainer with mailbox, registered office, Companies Office filings, annual return management, and register maintenance is typically USD 1,200 to USD 3,500 per annum.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 to USD 12,000 for a first-time certified independent audit of a near-threshold NZ limited company operating a data-pipeline and API-commerce business; an unaudited financial statement compilation or review for a small exempt API-commerce company typically costs USD 800 to USD 2,800.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand uses a single national corporate tax rate of 28%; it has no local or state corporate income tax. Effective tax relief arises from the full imputation system, the 15% New Zealand R&D tax incentive, the approved issuer levy 2% mechanism for certain listed interest, and treaty-integrated non-resident withholding tax reductions. No free-zone tax holidays or patent-box regimes are available in New Zealand. For this structured pipeline, the loss carryforward parameter is conservatively set to 5 years, while the Income Tax Act 2007 in fact permits indefinite carryforward of net losses to the extent the 49% shareholder continuity test is satisfied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return; lodged electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR portal or approved EDIS / gateway software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July following the income year; provisional tax is payable in three instalments during the year. For a non-standard balance date, the return must be filed by the last working day of the seventh month after balance date. Non-resident companies carrying on business through a New Zealand permanent establishment must file the IR4 together with the IR4S and the Schedule of Non-Resident Withholding Tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable income derived from all New Zealand sources, including commerce-scraping API gateway subscriptions, data licence fees, proxy access fees, Stripe settlement receipts, USDC-denominated revenue, interest, royalties, and other ordinary income, stated exclusive of GST.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company must include only income effectively connected with a New Zealand permanent establishment or derived from New Zealand sources. Related-party revenue recharged offshore must not be netted here; Inland Revenue will characterise the full contractual service fee according to substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses incurred in producing assessable income: cloud hosting, software development, bandwidth, employee remuneration, legal and compliance fees, AML screening software, and platform transaction costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All deductions must satisfy the business test and apportionment rules in s DA 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007. Management fees, IP royalties, and data purchasing charges paid to non-resident associates are deductible only to the extent they are arm's length, actually rendered, and not a disguised dividend.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss before taxation as reconciled from the statutory financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The accounting net profit must be reconciled from the New Zealand entity's own books. Where the New Zealand entity is deliberately under-margined due to repeat USDC buy-ins by an offshore parent, the IRD may disregard the accounting presentation and reconstruct the arm's length profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenditure and tax adjustments: 50% of non-exempt entertainment costs, fines, bribes, penalties, capital losses, non-deductible dual-purpose expenditure, and expenditure that is statistically capital in nature.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty exemption is not claimed in this box. A non-resident's DTA protection must be evidenced through a valid treaty certificate and beneficial ownership declaration; the taxable profit remains in the IR4 until formally excluded by the applicable double tax agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing and base erosion adjustment: increases or decreases to taxable income reflecting the arm's length principle for controlled cross-border transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the commerce-scraping API business is sold through a web of related overseas entities, the New Zealand company must apply the Income Tax Act 2007 subpart GC transfer pricing rules. A compensating adjustment must be made if the New Zealand entity was undercharged or overcharged for data, IP, management services, or capital.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses offset: current-year net loss and losses carried forward from earlier years, subject to the shareholder continuity test.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned New Zealand Limited must attach a continuity schedule proving that at least 49% of beneficial ownership has been maintained from loss year to current year. Cryptocurrency token transfers that change ultimate beneficial ownership can break continuity; full captable documentation must be preserved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after the application of all allowed loss offsets and adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This box must be non-negative. If transfer pricing adjustments are disputed, the company should still file with its best-available facts and use the schedules to explain the computation; failure to disclose an adjustment can trigger a 100% abusive-tax-position shortfall penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income tax assessed: taxable income multiplied by the 28% corporate income tax rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No concessional free-zone rate applies. A New Zealand branch of a foreign company using the PAYE, provisional tax, and resident withholding tax system should use the same 28% rate on attributable New Zealand-source profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credits, resident withholding tax credits, foreign tax credits, and any tax credits attaching to the company's income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should not receive imputation credits attached to distributed profits unless the distribution is fully imputed by the New Zealand payer. Any claimed foreign tax credits must be supported by evidence of foreign tax paid and must not exceed the New Zealand tax on the income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual income tax, terminal tax payable, or refund due after applying provisional tax and available credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company must account for New Zealand-sourced income even if no New Zealand tax is payable due to treaty relief. The correct terminal tax date must be observed; terminal tax underpaid as a result of omitted NRWT is subject to late payment penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of non-resident withholding tax on dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-residents during the income year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every outgoing dividend, interest payment, or royalty related to the commerce-scraping API must be reported. If the recipient claims a reduced treaty rate, the IR43 certificate and Tax Residency Certificate must be quoted; otherwise the statutory 30% dividend, 15% interest, and 15% royalty NRWT applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional disclosure schedules for related-party transactions, transfer pricing documentation, and economic substance indicators.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZ$5 million, mandatory transfer pricing documentation must be held and made available on request. The schedule should record the location of board meetings, employee decision-makers, server assets, management functions, and risk assumption to prove the New Zealand company is not a bare shell.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: A company that fails to file the IR4 on time may incur a late filing penalty of NZ$250 and an additional NZ$250 for each month or part month the return remains unfiled. Late payment of residual income tax attracts an initial late payment penalty of 1% and can escalate monthly. Shortfall penalties range from 20% for lack of reasonable care to 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. Knowingly filing a false IR4 is a criminal offence under the Tax Administration Act 1994 s 143, carrying a fine of up to NZ$50,000 and imprisonment for up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% under New Zealand non-resident withholding tax rules; treaty relief commonly reduces this to 15% for portfolio shareholders and 5% for direct shareholders holding at least 10% of the voting power, with 0% available for fully conduit and treaty-exempt dividend flows where beneficial ownership is proven.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident recipient must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) / Certificate of Residence from the foreign competent tax authority, complete Inland Revenue Form IR43 or its electronic treaty certificate equivalent, deliver it to the New Zealand payer before payment, and provide a written beneficial ownership declaration. The payer must verify that the recipient is the true beneficial owner and not a conduit. The certificate must be renewed annually or upon any change in circumstances and retained for 10 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on interest is 15% and on royalties 15%. Under many New Zealand DTAs, the interest rate is reduced to 10% and in certain treaty networks to 0% for approved bank interest, while royalties are commonly reduced to 10% or 5% for software / data licensing. The 2% Approved Issuer Levy may substitute for NRWT on interest paid by an approved New Zealand issuer to an unrelated non-resident lender. A New Zealand payer of data-scraping API royalties to an offshore licensor must withhold at source unless a valid IR43 and TRC support a lower treaty rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Cross-border related-party transactions of NZ$5.0 million or more in an income year trigger mandatory transfer pricing documentation (Local File). A group with consolidated annual revenue of NZ$1.125 billion or more is required to prepare a Master File and Country-by-Country Report. Even below these thresholds, the New Zealand taxpayer must hold contemporaneous records sufficient to demonstrate arm's length pricing for API subscriptions, data licensing, hosted services, and intercompany management charges.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not administer a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations statute; instead, substance is evaluated through the Income Tax Act 2007 general anti-avoidance rule s BG 1, business test in s DA 1, permanent establishment attribution under double tax agreements, and the New Zealand source rules. A company holding the nominal right to web-scraping API income but lacking Core Income-Generating Activities in New Zealand, such as board meetings, employee operators, client contracting, and central risk management, will be treated as a conduit: profits will be reallocated to the jurisdiction performing the true functions, imputation credit benefits may be denied, and NRWT will be imposed on payments made to the offshore principal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Sham Shell Company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The NZ Ltd is inserted into the commerce-scraping API enterprise purely as an invoicing shell with no office, no staff, and no business operations. It charges its BVI-related parent only a cost-plus fee for API gateway subscriptions while the BVI entity resells the same data access at a materially higher price and retains the profit in a zero-tax jurisdiction. Dividends and royalties are never declared and no residual New Zealand tax is paid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2007 s BG 1 disregards the tax avoidance arrangement; transfer pricing rules in ss GC 1-GC 20 impose an arm's length reallocation of profit. Tax Administration Act 1994 s 141(2C) imposes a 100% abusive-tax-position shortfall penalty, and s 143 imposes criminal fines of up to NZ$50,000 and imprisonment for up to 5 years for deliberate evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Companies Act 1993 s 189, the court may pierce the corporate veil if the company is used for fraud or tax evasion. Directors are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of the unpaid tax plus interest and penalties. Inland Revenue may obtain a travel-ban order preventing directors from leaving New Zealand until the debt is settled, and criminal conviction can disqualify the director from managing a company and trigger asset forfeiture of proceeds held in Stripe accounts or USDC wallets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Abusive DTA Relief
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The NZ Ltd pays a large notional software royalty or dividend to a Hong Kong related company without deducting NRWT. The Hong Kong recipient has no office, employees, or active business function, and the only tax benefit is an attempt to channel income through a lower-tax jurisdiction. No IR43 certificate, Tax Residency Certificate, or beneficial ownership declaration is ever prepared.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NRWT is imposed under Income Tax Act 2007 ss RF 8 and RF 9 and is payable by the payer under s RNA 8. Failure to deduct results in the New Zealand company being assessed for the full NRWT, plus a 150% evasion shortfall penalty under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and late payment penalties. Making a false treaty claim is an offence punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine of up to NZ$50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly direct the non-payment of NRWT are personally liable for the unremitted foreign withholding tax. Civil remedies include personal assessment, garnishment of USDC assets, and restitution of the tax shortfall. Criminal liability extends to imprisonment, travel bans, director disqualification, and forfeiture of the benefit obtained from the fraudulent treaty claim.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering Breach and Digital Payment Anonymisation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The commerce-scraping API gateway accepts Stripe card payments and USDC from wholesale purchasers without conducting customer due diligence, beneficial ownership verification, sanctioned-party screening, or transaction monitoring. The API is used by shell entities to scrape commercial data for sanctioned third parties, and the New Zealand Limited fails to register under the AML/CFT regime as a financial service provider.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 imposes civil penalties of up to NZ$2 million per contravention on a body corporate, and directors or senior managers may be subject to individual civil penalties of up to NZ$300,000. Failure to register as an AML/CFT reporting entity is a continuing offence. If the disseminated funds are criminal property, prosecution under Crimes Act 1961 ss 243-245 for money laundering carries imprisonment for up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly or recklessly facilitates the AML breach can be held personally liable for civil penalties and for restitution of laundered funds. The corporate veil may be pierced under Companies Act 1993 s 189 where the company is used as an instrument of financial crime. The director may be subject to travel bans, seizure of digital assets, disqualification from directorship for up to 5 years, and criminal imprisonment for money laundering.
